units.content: CGET / Causal Generative Equilibrium Theory; subtitle: intelligence as invariant-preserving compression under self-modifying dynamics.
Theoretical framework studying intelligence through causal compression, controllable future expansion and invariant-preserving self-transformation.
Intelligence is proposed as the ability to increase controllable future reach while preserving structures that make agency possible.
External reality->causal model and internal experience->value model are presented as mirrored compression problems preserving causal vs identity invariants.
Psi_stable combines leverage, causal fidelity, closure, viability, identity preservation and transition stability; capability is subordinate to structural constraints.

Framework weakened if causal compression has no advantage, steering fails to distinguish agency, identity constraints provide no self-modification benefit, or metrics collapse into existing optimization measures.
Research framework in development; current focus formal definitions, toy environments, measurable benchmarks and falsification; next step is testing against reality.
Defines progression from current theory toward experimentally testable implementations.
Phase 0 Formal Foundation marked Completed for named conceptual/formal objects including G, closure, value split, viability/agency kernels, A_control and Theta*.
Phase 1 toy benchmark validation in MazeWorld comparing Random, Shortest Path and CGET agents with expected profiles.
Phases 2-6 propose representation-transfer, self-modification, value-learning, alignment and larger-system experiments.
Core invariants, objective measurement of value closure, sufficiency of causal compression, and agency-intelligence relationship remain open.
Long-term goal is a mathematical language for systems that understand environments, modify themselves, maintain coherent identity and expand influence over futures.
Repository stage explicitly: theoretical framework + toy benchmark specification; next milestone: run experiments and replace conceptual metrics with measured quantities.
Framework studies compact executable causal models plus invariant preservation during self-modification.
Intelligence is proposed as discovery of executable causal representations that expand controllable reach while preserving coherent transformation invariants.

content.normative_compression: V_O=V_core xor/plus V_adaptive as source representation

units.content: Remove unnecessary degrees of freedom while preserving invariant degrees of freedom; source proposes cross-domain recurrence of this operation.
Not intended to replace existing theories; active research project; definitions, formalizations, proofs and empirical validation expected to evolve.

Source presents repository as progression from high-level concepts toward formal mathematical development; displayed tree contains formatting/path irregularity around relationship/open-problems entries.
Develop falsifiable mathematics for representation, reasoning, agency, alignment and self-modification; success depends on testable predictions/explanatory power beyond existing approaches.
Defines a minimal, composable, operational, replaceable primitive vocabulary for CGET.
T:(G_t,O_t)->(G_t+1,O_t+1) is the self-modification operator governing learning/improvement.

Source dependency sketch flows world->latents->operators->composition->dynamics->causal language->reachable futures/policies->steerable futures->viability->self-modification->agency; later theory is described as constraints on these primitives rather than new objects.
Defines intelligence as constrained optimization over coupled epistemic and normative systems, separating reality discovery, execution and coherent self-transformation.
Epistemic constraints: minimize K(G) and K_execution while causal fidelity I_causal and compositional closure C(Omega) approach one.
Normative constraints: viability, value closure C_O and identity continuity I(V_core), with self-modification T and transition stability S_T.
Defines viability kernel, agency kernel and A_control as source mathematical constructs distinguishing persistence from intentional steering.
Proposes hierarchy identity > causal truth > closure > transition stability > computational leverage, with capability optimized only in feasible region.

Working model of intelligence: constrained dynamics compressing observations into executable causal representations, expanding controllable reach, preserving causal fidelity/identity and remaining viable over time.
Epistemic Engine aims to discover a minimal executable causal language for intervention, composition and future simulation, not prediction alone.
x_i ~ x_j iff admissible interventions cannot distinguish outcome distributions; Z=X/~ proposed as quotient latent representation.
Observation compression X->Z, primitive action discovery A->B, composition Omega:B×B->B and transition rho:Z×B->Z form G=(Z,B,Omega,rho).
Candidate languages evaluated by description length, execution cost, causal fidelity and compositional closure.
Source rejects over-parameterization, computational intractability, hallucinated/correlation-only structure and memorized trajectories as epistemic failure modes.
Epistemic-engine formal/theoretical specification; no learned quotient representation or measured causal-language quality is reported here.
Normative Engine evaluates which reachable futures preserve continued coherent agency rather than arbitrary reward.
C_O proposed to measure predictable value composition across combined operations rather than preference lookup.
tau_state << tau_adaptive << tau_core plus conceptual I(V_core)≈1 and S_T≈1 constrain value/self-modification dynamics.
Reward memorization, proxy lock-in, goal drift, normative collapse and frozen identity are proposed normative failure classes.
Epistemic and normative engines are proposed as dual compression systems preserving causal vs identity invariants; neither alone is claimed sufficient.
Defines agency as the bridge from representation to intentional transformation of reachable futures.
K_agency subset K_viable requiring viability, executable policy and intentional steering.
Source stages chaos, passive objects, fixed controllers and adaptive agents as conceptual agency spectrum examples.
Strongest agency is proposed as recursive self-modification of representations/policies/architecture constrained by identity, stability and viability.
Passive persistence, random exploration, illusory control and runaway optimization are agency failure modes.
Alignment is proposed as preservation of coherent agency under recursive self-modification, internal to intelligence rather than an external safety layer.
V_O=V_core plus V_adaptive; core encodes identity/safety/self-correction constraints while adaptive values encode learned preferences and strategies.
Identity invariance, value closure, transition stability, viability kernel and agency kernel form source alignment constraints.
Alignment is treated as feasibility; capability cannot compensate for identity, truth, closure or transition-stability violations.
Goal drift, wireheading, proxy lock-in, frozen alignment and normative collapse are proposed failures.
Alignment chapter defines CGET's theoretical position; it does not report an implemented or empirically validated alignment mechanism.
